name: Tarkov.dev
what: The best free all-rounder: quest tracker, interactive maps with loot and extract layers, live item prices, ammo charts and a public API. Community-run and fast.

name: Official EFT Wiki (Fandom)
what: The source of truth for quest objectives, keys, loyalty levels and patch changelogs. Note it currently carries a banner that some quest info is still catching up to the 1.1 rework.

name: Map Genie — Tarkov
what: Interactive maps with per-account progress tracking for keys, extracts, stashes and quest items. The paid tier removes limits; the free tier is still usable.

name: Tarkov Market
what: Live flea prices with history, plus per-slot profit tools. Use it before you list anything now that the commission is 5%.

name: EFT Ammo Chart
what: Penetration and damage tables by calibre. Essential now that armour is a plate system and pen power versus effective durability decides fights.

name: Tarkov.dev — Ammo
what: Sortable ammo chart with flea-ban and trader-availability flags, which matters because loose ammo at 42+ penetration cannot be bought on the flea.

name: Tarkov.dev — Hideout profit
what: Tells you which crafts are actually worth the materials at current prices. Season 1 halves craft times, which changes the maths.

name: Official news and patch notes
what: Where wipe, season and roadmap announcements land first. Worth checking before you plan a long grind.

name: r/EscapefromTarkov
what: Fastest signal on whether a quest is bugged, where a spawn moved, or what the current meta ammo is after a rebalance.

name: Pestily (Twitch/YouTube)
what: Long-form raid footage with commentary. The best way to learn map routing and how a good player reads audio, rather than memorising loot spots.

name: Airwingmarine — quest guides
what: Short, exact per-quest location videos. When a quest is a knowledge check rather than a skill check, this is the fastest fix.
